In November my roommate and good friend bought decorative gem corn at Walmart to put on her Dia De Los Muertos altar. When she was going to throw them away a few weeks later I decided to strip the cobs of their kernels to see if they would grow. They did. This collage brings them from when they first sprouted up to about 5 feet tall. Now they're sprouting ears of corn and have made a really nice trellis for my third generation Noodle Beans, the original seeds I brought back from Laos 2 summers ago.

I also have several basils, which out of all my plants, thrive in this humid Louisiana heat. My pumpkins and tomatoes all died :(

They are purple ruffle, genovese, and thai basils. From top left to bottom right shows them from their first planting until now.

The back patio in my condo complex is small, so I try and keep my pots and plants from overwhelming the neighbors, but I also have a few other things growing like this wild fennel I collected and planted, growing with what will soon be a cilantro sea, some scattered marigolds, unknown basil variety, kale, other beans, and hopefully in a few months I'll have lovely chilies to show off.
That is amazing how you grew so much in a limited space. Your corn grew so nicely. Very efficient.
